title: Design of altermagnetism in oxide superlattices exploiting interface effects and quantum confinement
abstract: The discovery of altermagnetism has initiated intensive research and opened new avenues for spin- tronic and transport applications. While current efforts are mostly focused on bulk materials which are typically insulating, here we propose design strategies to achieve a combination of altermag- netism and metallicity in oxide superlattices by exploiting symmetry breaking, electrostatic doping and confinement. While bulk SrCrO3 does not exhibit altermagnetism due to compensating effects between adjacent layers our density functional theory calculations with a Hubbard U parameter re- veal, that a single SrCrO3 layer confined in a (SrCrO3)1/(SrTiO3)1(001) superlattice (SL) exhibits a sizable non-relativistic spin splitting (NRSS) up to 350 meV with bulk d-wave nature due to the coexistence of orbital ordering and octahedral rotations (OORs). Since this system is insulating, we extend to SrCrO3/LaCrO3(001) SLs. In the (SrCrO3)4/(LaCrO3)4(001) SL the combination of a polar discontinuity at the interface and stronger OORs promotes metallic d-wave altermagnetism. The NRSS of up to 120 meV is contributed by the interfacial Cr d bands at the Fermi level with indications for a spin-selective Fermi surface nesting. These findings establish oxide superlattices as a promising platform to realize and explore altermagnetism for quantum transport and spintronic functionalities
summary: This theoretical study proposes that oxide superlattices are excellent platforms for realizing metallic altermagnetism. By engineering interfaces between perovskites like $	ext{SrCrO}_3$ and $	ext{LaCrO}_3$, the authors overcome bulk limitations to induce significant spin splitting (NRSS) in the electronic bands. This work guides the design of next-generation materials for quantum transport applications.
main_problem: The primary goal is designing materials that exhibit altermagnetism (spin-polarized band splitting in compensated antiferromagnets) while maintaining metallic conductivity for spintronic applications.
main_result: Oxide superlattices, particularly $	ext{(SrCrO}_3	ext{)/(LaCrO}_3	ext{)}_n$, are shown to be promising platforms that can realize robust metallic d-wave altermagnetism by exploiting interface effects and structural distortions.
method: The study employs Density Functional Theory calculations, specifically incorporating a Hubbard U parameter (DFT+U), to model the electronic structure of these complex oxide superlattices.
model_or_system: The research focuses on perovskite oxide superlattices like $	ext{(SrCrO}_3	ext{)/(SrTiO}_3	ext{)}_1(001)$ and $	ext{(SrCrO}_3	ext{)/(LaCrO}_3	ext{)}_n(001)$. These systems are engineered to break symmetry and induce electronic reconstruction at the interfaces.
key_observables: Non-Relativistic Spin Splitting (NRSS) magnitude (up to 350 meV), spin-polarized band structures, spin-split Fermi surfaces (FSs), and metallic character derived from interfacial Cr $d$ bands.
important_parameters: The Hubbard U parameter ($U$), the number of repeating units ($n$), and structural distortions like octahedral rotations (OORs) are critical parameters explored.
main_assumptions: Bulk $	ext{SrCrO}_3$ is limited by compensating effects, necessitating the use of superlattices to achieve observable altermagnetism. The metallic state relies on interfacial electronic reconstruction driven by polar discontinuity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spin-polarized band structures showing the emergence of NRSS in various SLs and schematic representations detailing structural distortions (JT/OORs) associated with different magnetic phases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical challenge—achieving altermagnetism plus metallicity. It then analyzes specific superlattice designs, comparing bulk behavior to confined systems ($	ext{SrTiO}_3$ and $	ext{LaCrO}_3$ interfaces), detailing how structural/polar discontinuities enable large NRSS values.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses advanced electronic structure calculations (DFT+U) on complex correlated oxides to predict functional quantum materials, directly addressing mechanisms for spin-charge coupling crucial in modern spintronics and condensed matter theory.
